evidence: Petr. 103: immō potius facite quod jubeō
Plaut. Aul. 153: hoc face quod tē jubet soror
Plaut. Bacch. 990a: Taceās: quod jubeō id faciās.
terms.comment: Petronius has the plural, Plautus the old form face and the subjunctive faciās; the singular Fac quod jubeō is the same sentence. The answer is Faciam (quod jubēs)., as in Plaut. Men. 850.

terms.gloss: be obedient, do as you’re told
terms.grammar: dictō audiēns esse (+ dative of the person)
evidence: Plaut. Amph. 989: ego sum Jovī dictō audiēns
terms.comment: The set phrase for obedience, with the dative of the one obeyed; see “obedient”. The command with estō is ours on that phrase.

evidence: Plaut. Bacch. 438–439: quam magistrō dēsinēbat esse dictō oboediēns

phrases.english: Do as you’re told: put your shoes on.

phrases.latin: Potin’ animō ut sīs quiētō et faciās quod jubeō?
phrases.english: Can you keep calm and do as I tell you?
Be quiet: do as I tell you.

phrases.latin: nam ōlim populī prius honōrem capiēbat suffrāgiō, quam magistrō dēsinēbat esse dictō oboediēns
phrases.english: for in the old days a boy won office by the people’s vote before he stopped doing what his teacher told him

sources: Lewis & Short: jubeo · Lewis & Short: dictum · Lewis & Short: audiens · Lewis & Short: oboedio
